ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information (Joint Order No. 3 [2024] of the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, effective 1 November 2024); Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, as amended); and mandatory beneficial ownership identification rules under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registrar / Registry of Companies in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention member state path: notarize if required; obtain Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority of the issuing state; then arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member state path: notarize if required; obtain authentication from the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs or equivalent; obtain consular legalization from the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China; then arrange certified Chinese translation. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry / Registrar of Companies in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention member state path: notarize if required; obtain Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member state path: notarize; obtain MFA authentication; obtain consular legalization from the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China; arrange certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent management body of the foreign investor/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention member state path: notarize the resolution and obtain Hague Apostille from the competent authority; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member state path: notarize; authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; obtain consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate; arrange certified Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or constitutional equivalent) of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder company, certified by its registered agent or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention member state path: notarize the certified copy and obtain Hague Apostille; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member state path: notarize; authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; obtain consular legalization from the Chinese Embassy/Consulate; arrange certified Chinese translation. Use only one authentication path per instrument; never chain both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the foreign shareholder's commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate account bank of the foreign investor/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention member state path: have the bank officer's signature notarized and obtain Hague Apostille from the relevant competent authority; arrange certified Chinese translation. Non-member state path: have the signature notarized, then obtain MFA authentication and consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate; arrange certified Chinese translation. The two paths are alternative, not cumulative.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, proposed legal representative, director, supervisor, senior manager, authorized signatory, and major counterparty of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must be screened before incorporation and at least quarterly thereafter against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists, EU and UK HM Treasury consolidated lists, and China's domestic AML watchlists and court dishonest-debtor blacklist. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory if the individual is a politically exposed person, a domestic high-ranking public official, or a family member or close associate of such person. Screening must use fuzzy matching, phonetic and transliteration variations, ID and passport verification, and source-of-funds evidence; any red flag must be escalated, documented, and cleared by the AML compliance officer before capital contribution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration and Name Pre-Clearance Portal / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration, a Chinese company name must be composed of standard simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier statutory structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or operation characteristics + legal form. The foreign investor's corporate name must be transliterated into Mandarin Chinese phonetics using standard simplified characters; English or Latin script is permitted only in the separately registered English name or as an approved additional trade name and may not replace the Chinese name. The distinctive part shall not be confusingly similar to an existing enterprise name and must not be composed solely of numerals, letters, pinyin, or misleading terms. The proposed transliteration must match the investor's certificate of incorporation and must be supported by a certified translation where required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name clearance system rejects a proposed name, the applicant shall first preserve the official electronic rejection notice. The applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the market regulation authority at the next higher level within 60 days of receipt of the rejection, or may file an administrative lawsuit directly with the competent People's Court within six months after becoming aware of the rejection. Alternatively, the applicant may revise the proposed Chinese name by removing any prohibited or sensitive token, adding a more distinctive component, or obtaining the required prior approval from the State Council or competent sectoral authority for a name containing 'China' or 'National', and then re-submit through the SAMR portal. Any resubmission starts a fresh 30-day reservation window; appeal deadlines are strict and non-waivable.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Chapter II on Incorporation of Limited Liability Companies, together with the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), particularly Articles 26, 28 and 34, and the Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Supervision Administration at the intended registered office, acting through the National Enterprise Registration System and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of an Enterprise as a Legal Person (foreign-invested limited liability company), accompanied by the Articles of Association and the Foreign Investment Information Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None; under the PRC Company Law and Foreign Investment Law, no statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture engaged in ISIC 7490 consulting; shareholders determine the registered capital in the Articles of Association and pay it according to an agreed capital contribution schedule. No blocked escrow account is required by law, but contribution funds received in China must be held in a bank account at a commercial bank licensed by the People's Bank of China and reported through the foreign investment information reporting system.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: FIRST, that the shareholders present, constituting the entire body of subscribers to the formation of Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Limited (the Company), do hereby adopt, ratify and approve the Company's Articles of Association in the form presented to this meeting, including the subscribed registered capital and the detailed capital contribution schedule annexed thereto; the total registered capital shall be paid by the shareholders in accordance with the schedule set out in the Articles, it being acknowledged that the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law do not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited liability consulting company, and that the Directors may open a dedicated capital contribution receiving account with a commercial bank licensed by the People's Bank of China for the purpose of receiving subscription funds, but no blocked escrow arrangement is required by law. SECOND, that the registered office of the Company located at the address stated in the Articles of Association, lawfully leased and available for the Company's registered address, be and the same is hereby adopted as the legal seat and address of the Company for all corporate, regulatory, tax and judicial service purposes, and the officers are directed to cause the office lease, property ownership or leasing registration certificate and usage documentation to be maintained in the corporate minute book and to file any required address declarations with the competent Market Supervision Administration upon establishment. THIRD, that the following natural persons be and they are hereby appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company: the designated Chairman as Executive Director and Legal Representative; the designated General Manager; the designated Finance Controller and Chief Financial Officer; and the designated Supervisor. Each appointee shall assume office as of the date of issuance of the Company's Business License and shall serve subject to the Company Law, the Articles, and the Foreign Investment Law until earlier succession or removal. FOURTH, that the General Manager and Chairman, acting jointly or severally, be and they are hereby authorized to execute and submit the enterprise establishment registration application to the State Administration for Market Regulation, to procure the Unified Social Credit Code certificate, to arrange the engraving of the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal and legal representative seal, to complete tax registration with the State Taxation Administration and social insurance registration, and to perform all post-registration filings. FIFTH, that the corporate bank account, including a RMB basic deposit account and, if required, a foreign exchange settlement account, be established at the bank designated by the Board, with authorized signatories being the General Manager and the Finance Controller; all payments shall follow a dual-signature rule above the threshold set by the Board; all SWIFT and wire transfers shall be subject to anti-money-laundering screening and customer due diligence procedures, and any cross-border fees shall be borne by the Company. SIXTH, that the officers are directed to implement all internal controls for international anti-dumping trade defense consulting clients and to comply with the Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting, so that the venture may lawfully commence business operations immediately after licensing; this resolution shall be effective immediately and copies shall be filed with the registered office and recorded in the first board minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Documentation Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service; local Market Supervision Administration for name reservation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an enterprise name pre-approval through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service of SAMR, selecting a name composed of trade-name, industry description and legal form; simultaneously verify that the proposed business scope of international anti-dumping trade defense consulting is not within the Foreign Investment Negative List. Prepare and notarize the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, passport identity documents, and power of attorney, together with a Chinese language translation. Draft the Articles of Association, capital contribution schedule, legal representative appointment resolution, and foreign investment information report. Submit the name application and await issuance of a Name Pre-Approval Notice.
required_dossiers: Proposed enterprise name and name structure
Identification documents of each shareholder, and for a foreign entity its certificate of incorporation, passport ID, power of attorney, apostille or Chinese consular legalization
Draft Articles of Association
Proposed capital contribution schedule
Proposed business scope description covering ISIC 7490 trade defense consulting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, promptly submit a new name with alternative trade-name choices; if a correction query is raised, use the SAMR online response channel within 15 working days and include the missing documents; no administrative appeal is required unless registration is denied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment Registration Application and SAMR Legal Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration at the intended registered office; online filing through the SAMR enterprise registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment registration application and supporting dossiers to the local Market Supervision Administration where the registered office is located, either through the online portal or by attending the enterprise registration window. The application must include the completed Application for Establishment Registration of an Enterprise as a Legal Person, the Articles of Association in Chinese, appointment instruments, lease contract, property ownership proof, and identity files. SAMR will conduct legality and compliance review under the Company Law, check the foreign investment information report and Negative List status, and, if no objection, enter the company in the enterprise registry and issue a paper and electronic Business License with a Unified Social Credit Code. The applicant should monitor the registry website for any correction notices.
required_dossiers: Name Pre-Approval Notice
Notarized or legalized foreign investor documentation
Articles of Association executed by all shareholders
Appointment instrument for Legal Representative, Executive Directors, Supervisor, and General Manager
Lease contract for registered office and property ownership proof
Identity documents of all officers and shareholders
Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, rectify within the statutory 15-working-day correction period; if denied, request a written denial reason, file administrative reconsideration or reapply with corrected Articles; contact the SAMR window for procedural cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business License Issuance and Company Seal Engraving and Recordation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Business License issuance window; Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving center for official seal recordation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Business License is issued, arrange for the engraving of the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, legal representative seal and, where necessary, contract seal at a licensed seal carver with the applicable Public Security Bureau seal recordation. The legal representative must attend or provide written authorization and identity documentation; each seal impression is recorded and entered into the public security seal database. Collect the original seals and maintain a seal-use log. Thereafter, the legal representative should update signatures, execute the bank opening resolution, and begin preparing for tax invoicing by applying for invoice quota and VAT status at the tax authority. Seal files must match the registered corporate name exactly.
required_dossiers: Original Business License of the Company
Legal Representative identity document
Written authorization where seal application is made by an agent
Company seal, financial seal, invoice seal and legal representative seal engraving order
Registered office address and Unified Social Credit Code details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal recordation is rejected or delayed, require the engraving shop to correct the offline record and refile with the Public Security Bureau; if seal-name mismatch occurs, request a return and re-engrave before any execution is made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Social Insurance Registration and Accounting System Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local tax office; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; SAMR integrated data exchange.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon obtaining the Unified Social Credit Code, complete tax registration at the local State Taxation Administration office; although data are shared through SAMR, the general manager must submit taxpayer registration information, choose general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer status, report the finance director, and apply for invoicing and e-invoice raising. Within 30 days of establishment, complete social insurance registration for employees with the local human resources and social security bureau and report payroll; the company must simultaneously register at the local labor inspection platform if required. The accountants shall adopt the PRC Accounting Standards, establish books, and file monthly or quarterly tax returns from the first month of operation. Office leases should be retained for fidelity and deduction purposes.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code
Legal Representative and Finance Controller identity documents
Articles of Association and First Board Resolution
Office lease contract
Employee roster and payroll policies
Bank account details after opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social insurance registration is questioned, file written explanations with the local tax bureau or social security center and provide evidence; late registration may be cured by voluntary disclosure and payment of any minor administrative penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Foreign Exchange Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the People's Bank of China; State Administration of Foreign Exchange acting through designated bank agents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a RMB basic deposit account with a commercial bank in China and, if requested, a foreign currency settlement account for receiving SWIFT and wire transfers from clients. The resolution appointing signatories, the Articles, business license, seal set, and officer and beneficial ownership identification are submitted to the bank's legal and compliance department. The bank will perform customer due diligence and anti-money-laundering screening, set dual-signature rules, and report the foreign shareholder's foreign exchange information to SAFE through the bank as agent. Foreign investors must receive capital contributions after the establishment date; inward remittance can be reported in the foreign investment information report. The bank should be instructed to scan each wire for sanctions and anti-dumping case-related payments.
required_dossiers: Original Business License
Company seal set and legal representative seal
Articles of Association and corporate bank account Board Resolution
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Identity documents of signatories and beneficial officers
Foreign investor documentation for AML/KYC review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence or freezes remittance, provide beneficial ownership charts, source-of-funds documentation, board approval and KYC supplements; unresolved suspension may be escalated to the People's Bank of China complaint channel or to another bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Final Foreign Investment Report and Commencement of Trade Defense Consulting Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation and Ministry of Commerce Foreign Investment Information Reporting System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the prescribed statutory reporting window, submit the foreign investment information report through the SAMR and Ministry of Commerce online reporting platform, covering shareholding changes, capital payments, and actual control; retain registrations in the corporate authorization. Complete the corporate minute book with the first board resolution, subscription schedules, meeting records, seal register, equity certificates, and capital verification records if any. Confirm that no industrial or environmental operating license is required for ISIC 7490 professional consulting because there is no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operation. Before commencing client service, verify that the general Business License has been obtained; if the venture intends to provide PRC-law legal opinions or represent clients before Chinese authorities, a separate law firm license and qualified PRC lawyers would be required.
required_dossiers: All formation and registration certificates
Foreign Investment Information Report acknowledgment
First Board Resolution and minute book
Seal recordation certificates
Bank account confirmation and signatory form
Business license and tax registration certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment information report is late or queried, submit it as soon as identified using the voluntary correction function and pay any nominal administrative penalty; maintain timeline evidence and file written responses through the reported authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), Department of Enterprise Registration, as the general commercial licensing authority; Ministry of Justice is relevant only if the joint venture seeks to provide licensed PRC law practice, which is not part of the ISIC 7490 consulting scope unless separately licensed.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License for Enterprise as Legal Person (Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company), bearing the Unified Social Credit Code; no separate industrial manufacturing, assembly, chemical, or warehousing operating permit is required for ISIC 7490 professional consulting.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China (MEE) - not applicable for ISIC 7490 professional consulting, so no agency filing or approval is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable; the activity is not listed under the Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessments and involves no construction, industrial production, chemical handling, or physical project undertaking.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to operations; there is no industrial wastewater, VOC emission, hazardous waste, noise, or combustion source. Office premises must comply only with municipal sanitary sewer connection, solid waste sorting, and indoor environmental hygiene requirements applicable to non-industrial leased offices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for industrial or hazardous occupancy; the leased office must maintain valid fire safety inspection and fire prevention clearance under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China and comply with workplace safety and occupational health obligations under the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China; no Civil Defense industrial fire permit, structural load inspection, or hazardous materials clearance is triggered for pure consulting use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) with its nationwide Electronic Tax Bureau (E-Tax) online portal accessible through www.chinatax.gov.cn; domestic administration is handled by the county-level tax service bureaus under the STA via the unified e-Tax platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture formed in China (Mainland), the entity will first complete business registration with the Administration for Market Regulation (AMR). The AMR issues a business license containing the Uniform Social Credit Code, which is the legal taxpayer identification number. The JV must then complete tax registration through the STA e-Tax portal within 30 days of business registration. The procurement procedure for a foreign non-resident entity without a permanent establishment is separate: the non-resident must apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) with the STA through the withholding agent or directly under the Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Registration procedure, supplying the enterprise incorporation certificate, foreign legal evidence, and a China contact person or fiscal representative. For the JV, the Unified Social Credit Code will be the sole TIN used for all State Tax Administration filings, VAT registration, export tax refunds, payroll/social insurance contributions, and anti-dumping trade-defense invoice issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not provide a check-the-box election, partnership pass-through election, or hybrid-mismatch election. Enterprise tax classification is dictated by the Enterprise Income Tax Law. The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income. The only relevant elections relate to special tax treatment for qualified asset restructuring under STA notices; those are not entity classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (5 million Renminbi) creates mandatory status as a VAT general taxpayer. Below this threshold a VAT taxpayer is treated as a small-scale taxpayer, but may elect to register as a general taxpayer. All enterprises that obtain a business license are automatically tax-registered regardless of the 5-million threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China enforces mandatory real-time electronic invoice clearance under the STA's Golden Tax System Phase IV. Invoicing must be done through the e-Tax platform or an authorized third-party electronic invoice service provider integrated by API. VAT invoices are the Full-Digital Electronic Invoice (All-Electronic Invoice) model; issuance sends invoice data in real time to the STA's tax control system, where the invoice is assigned a unique tax-control code, digitally signed, stamped, and QR-monitored. No physical stamped red invoices are permitted for trade-defense consulting and export transactions; digital anti-fraud is achieved by automatic code control, real-time invoice data reconciliation, purchaser verification, and mandatory electronic invoice archive.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, 0% VAT and the corresponding refund of input tax are available if the goods are customarily declared for export, leave China through a customs supervised area, and the export proceeds are repatriated in accordance with foreign-exchange regulations. For services, the trade-defense and legal-consulting services qualify for 0% VAT only when supplied to an overseas client, the recipient is located outside China, the services are wholly consumed outside China, and full documentation proves the cross-border supply. Anti-dumping trade-defense consulting services involving representation before Chinese authorities may not qualify for zero-rating where the place of supply is deemed domestic; only qualifying cross-border offshore services satisfy STA zero-rating criteria.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export goods customs declaration form) containing the export customs supervision number, HS classification, export quantity, value, exporter name, and consignee details
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing the export goods have been loaded and shipped from China to the overseas buyer

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange receipt/remittance record proving the export proceeds were received in convertible currency from the overseas buyer through the Chinese banking system
Export sales contract and commercial invoice showing the parties, terms of trade, pricing, and confirmation that the export sale is not a related-party sham transaction
Packing list and verified certificate of origin concerning the exported goods
Export goods VAT invoice or the digital electronic invoice issued for the export transaction
Customs agent power of attorney and customs release record, when clearance is undertaken via a customs broker
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and refund claims face rigorous audit scrutiny by the STA and Customs. If the tax authority determines that zero-rating was wrongly claimed due to insufficient, false, or contradictory documents, or if the export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory period, the entire VAT output tax deemed zero-rated is clawed back. For fraudulent refund claims, the Tax Administration Law imposes recovery of the unpaid tax plus penalties from 50% to five times the amount involved; late payment interest accrues and tax credits are disallowed. In criminal cases, the Criminal Law punishes export tax refund fraud by imprisonment of up to life plus fines. Administrative penalties also include temporary or permanent loss of export tax refund qualification, third-party liability for tax agents, and reassessment procedures without a limitation period for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), the foreign-exchange regulatory agency administered by the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains full convertibility on the current account for trade in goods and services, but the capital account remains administered by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE). RMB is not freely convertible on demand; every inbound and outbound flow must be supported by an underlying real transaction and, where required, a SAFE registration or bank-level verification. A Sino-foreign equity joint venture's injected capital is treated as capital-account income; it must be registered with SAFE under the foreign direct investment (FDI) registration process and may not be credited to any account other than the dedicated foreign-exchange capital account. Once the registered capital is settled into RMB and spent on operations, the JV may not arbitrarily repatriate the funds to offshore investors or redeploy them outside the approved business scope. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is classified under the current account as dividend distribution and is permitted only after audited financial statements, board resolution, tax withholding certificate, and tax clearance are submitted to the settlement bank. Service fees from anti-dumping trade-defense consulting are current-account receipts; the JV may retain such FX in its export settlement account or convert it at market rates for working capital. Practical compliance hurdles include SAFE's true-transaction review, bank-level documentation collection, and the absence of unrestricted access to offshore non-deliverable RMB products.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China does not impose a fixed mandatory surrender percentage or a fixed conversion ratio for export receipts. Under the current total-amount monitoring model, all export service receipts must be repatriated through the domestic banking system; the enterprise may retain 100% of the foreign exchange in its export settlement account or convert at market rates. The statutory verification framework is the SAFE Administrative Measures for the Administration of Foreign Exchange in Goods and Services Trade (2012, as amended); in bank practice, the receipt must be matched to the filed service-transaction declaration within the bank's monitoring period, typically 90 days from the contractual payment due date. If the bank flags an unmatched receipt, the entity must supply the original service contract, invoice, evidence of service delivery, and the export-service tax status, or the bank will suspend future cross-border payments. There is no statutory conversion quota for this category, but every settlement must be reflected in SAFE statistics.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and largely non-viable for onshore entity formation. Offshore digital EMI platforms, including foreign-licensed money-service businesses or e-money institutions, are not permitted to act as the domestic bank or hold the JV's registered capital onshore because the PBOC and SAFE recognize only licensed mainland banking institutions for foreign-exchange and RMB clearing. Domestic clients cannot lawfully maintain their operating account with an unlicensed offshore EMI; foreign-currency collection through such a platform is only permissible if the platform has a licensed mainland payment affiliate and operates under a PBOC payment license, and even then it cannot replace the direct bank relationship needed for SAFE reporting, tax matching, and capital verification. Use tier-1 banks only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is mandatory for the statutory legal representative. For a Chinese-mainland JV, the legal representative and an authorized signatory with financial-control authority must attend the branch onboarding interview in person, carrying the business license, original seals, board resolution for account opening, and passports or national IDs. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for statutory legal representatives. Non-resident shareholders may be represented by an authorized person in China under a notarized and consular-legalized power of attorney; however, the legal representative's physical interview, biometric capture, and dual-verification by bank officers remain non-waivable. Some bank branches accept video-verified account opening for extensions of existing relationships but not for fresh-entity KYC with FDI capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: foreign JV partner's capital origin or ultimate ownership is not transparent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Five-year corporate registration dossier of every direct shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), passport copies, UBO self-declaration, bank financial statements for the capital source, notarized share-purchase agreements, and a signed sworn statement identifying all persons holding 10% or more.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border legal-service revenue is perceived as trade-remedy circumvention or represents proceeds of tariff-fraud advisory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid PRC business license covering consultancy, foreign-investment license for relevant legal services, engagement letters that expressly limit deliverables to lawful defense in anti-dumping proceedings, MOFCOM and other authorities' case dockets, and a legal opinion from PRC counsel confirming that the services do not assist customs or tariff evasion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flows from high-risk jurisdictions or politically exposed persons involved in trade-policy matters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening reports generated from OFAC, EU, UN and FATF high-risk-country filters and PEP lists; identity cards and passports of client legal representatives, beneficial owners and case-contact personnel; source-of-funds declarations; client bank statements for the invoice amount; and a rationale memorandum establishing why a payment from a sanctioned jurisdiction is legitimate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential mismatch between injected capital and the entity's stated working-capital needs, which may signal layering or fake FDI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 24-month budget, the foreign-exchange registration certificate for FDI, shareholder loan agreements, third-party valuation of the project, rent and office leases, staffing contracts, and a cash-flow model tied to ISIC 7490 trade-defense advisory revenue.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 wire from the foreign shareholder to the JV's onshore foreign-exchange capital account at the chosen tier-1 bank. Remittance fields must quote the JV's legal name, SAFE FDI registration code, and the purpose code for equity injection. Upon arrival, the bank will place funds in the capital account and complete SAFE's capital-account-income settlement procedure, then issue a settlement note. The JV must instruct a Chinese certified public accountant to perform capital verification and issue a capital-verification report within the timeframe required by the SAFE registration and bank KYC file; this report, plus the SAFE registration and bank certificate, becomes the legal evidence of paid-in capital. For outbound return of unused capital or delayed investment, an additional SAFE exit registration is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For JV operational disbursements and payments to overseas anti-dumping defense counsel, the preferred clearing rail is the SWIFT MT103 message with clean proceeds and full purpose identification. If remittance is in RMB, use the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) rather than conventional SWIFT. For goods-based settlement in support of trade-defense exhibits or sample shipments, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit or documentary collection (documents against payment or documents against acceptance) is permitted. All outbound service-trade payments require the standard SAFE service-trade declaration, original contract, invoice, evidence of real service delivery, and tax withholding certificate where relevant. The bank will perform a pre-payment overflow check against accumulated settlement records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD forward contracts with a licensed domestic bank for genuine current-account receipts and disbursements, with tenors referencing the underlying service contracts
Onshore foreign-exchange swaps used for liquidity and settlement-point alignment in the JV's cross-border cash flow
SAFE-approved cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term exposures arising from FDI funding or major project financing
SAFE-approved vanilla FX options for hedging receivables from anti-dumping consulting clients, with no speculative or exotic options permitted

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not an onshore clearing rail for this entity; if made available synthetically through the bank's offshore branch, execution is strictly discouraged and would require regulatory approval due to mainland capital-control constraints

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Credit Information Report (Annual Declaration / Annual Return for all market entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; local Market Supervision Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 each year for the preceding calendar year; no anniversary-based extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No civil late fee is imposed, but failure to publish by June 30 places the entity on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days. If not corrected within 3 years, the entity is moved to the List of Seriously Illegal and Dishonest Enterprises; administrative restrictions on bank financing, tax invoice quotas, government procurement, and market access follow. Continued serious violations can lead to administrative revocation of the business license, and under PRC Company Law a company that has not commenced business for 6 consecutive months or has ceased business for 6 consecutive months may have its business license revoked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (applicable to Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) jointly collected through the SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 each year for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Foreign investors or the joint venture are ordered by MOFCOM to rectify within a specified time; refusal to rectify or false or missing reporting can trigger a fine of up to RMB 100,000 (approximately USD 14,000). Repeated non-reporting may be treated as a serious credit impairment and affect the enterprise's suitability for future administrative approvals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Payment Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) and the local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 immediately following each tax year-end (within 5 months of the fiscal year close)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return fines range from RMB 50 to RMB 2,000 (approximately USD 7 to USD 280); late payment surcharge accrues at 0.05% per day on the unpaid tax. Continued evasion may lead to tax lien and asset attachment, exit visa restrictions on the legal representative, administrative revocation of tax registration, and ultimately court compulsory collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Statutory Audit Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and Board of Directors of the joint venture; audit report is also submitted to tax and registration authorities when required and serves as the supporting schedule of the annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements must be audited within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year under the PRC Company Law; audit report should be completed before the June 30 annual report window closes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain an audit invalidates reliance on financial statements for profit distribution, may make the annual report false or incomplete, exposes directors and the legal representative to liability for inaccurate corporate declarations, and can result in administrative penalties up to RMB 100,000 (approximately USD 14,000) plus personal liability for losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Equity Transfer / Change of Registered Items and Shareholder Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local SAMR company registration authority; company's internal statutory register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after the effective date of the equity transfer or corporate change, including director, supervisor, and legal representative changes, under the PRC Company Registration Administration Regulations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration may draw a rectification order and a fine of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000 (approximately USD 1,400 to USD 14,000); use of false documents in such filings carries a fine of RMB 50,000 to RMB 500,000 (approximately USD 7,000 to USD 70,000) and possible revocation of the business license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law and the Accounting Law, every company legal person, including a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, must prepare annual financial reports and obtain an independent audit by a PRC-licensed CPA firm; there is no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption for company-form entities. Listed companies, security issuers, and enterprises with public fundraising obligations must also have their interim financial statements audited as prescribed by the CSRC and stock exchanges. Quantitative size classes are used to determine the accounting framework: a micro industrial enterprise has fewer than 20 employees and annual revenue below RMB 3 million; a small or medium industrial enterprise has 20 to fewer than 1,000 employees and annual revenue between RMB 3 million and RMB 400 million; a large enterprise has 1,000 or more employees or annual revenue of RMB 400 million or above. Micro and small or medium enterprises may apply the Simplified Accounting System for Small Enterprises, whereas large enterprises and all public-interest entities must apply full Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE) as substantively converged with IFRS. Regardless of classification, the joint venture remains subject to mandatory annual statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE) converged with IFRS; Simplified Accounting System for Small Enterprises (ASSE) may apply only to qualifying micro and small or medium enterprises; listed issuers apply CSRC-revised CAS.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 20% enterprise income tax rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises, which with the statutory 25% tax-base inclusion creates 5% effective rate on annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million; 15% preferential rate for High and New Technology Enterprises and for encouraged enterprises in the Western Regions; 100% super deduction of qualified research and development expenses; accelerated depreciation for fixed assets used in R&D; 10-year loss carryforward for eligible high-tech and small-medium science technology enterprises; and no separate patent box but royalty income may benefit from treaty relief or R&D expense deductions when substance is present.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A) referenced by STA return code A100000, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau portal; quarterly prepayment returns on STA Form A010000 are filed through the same portal with e-certificate authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment returns are due within 15 calendar days after the end of each quarter; the annual return and final tax settlement are due within 5 calendar months after the fiscal year-end, i.e. by 31 May for a calendar-year entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue, including sales of services, consulting fees, and other ordinary business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all China-source revenues derived by the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, including trade-remedy defense consulting fees paid by Chinese exporters; exclude offshore income not attributable to a Chinese permanent establishment; classify cross-border royalties, interest, and management fees separately for withholding and permanent establishment analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and direct operating costs incurred to generate revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only documented, arm's-length costs; disallow excessive service fees paid to foreign related parties that are not substantiated by contracts, actual activity, or a benefit test; maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing records to avoid upward adjustment of taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses, including employee compensation, rent, professional fees, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to non-resident related parties for advisory, management, or anti-dumping defense services are deductible only where the recipient has economic substance, the fee is at arm's length, and the service is actually rendered; otherwise the payment is recharacterized as a non-deductible distribution or royalty subject to withholding tax.

Reconcile quarterly prepayment, transfer pricing adjustments, and special tax adjustment notices; if the JV is deemed to have under-recognized revenue attributable to the Chinese operation, a special tax adjustment may be imposed with interest from the late payment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income, including government subsidies, debt waivers, insurance recoveries, and foreign exchange gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue as taxable China-source income any subsidies or rebates connected with the JV's domestic operations; foreign exchange gains from cross-border loans are included unless a specific exemption applies; failure to include these may trigger under-declaration penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenses, loss adjustments, and permanent differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reverse non-deductible items such as administrative fines, tax penalties, bribes, illegal fees, unverified impairment provisions, and portions of related-party interest exceeding thin-capitalization debt-equity limits; include special tax adjustment items from STA transfer pricing audits and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income before loss carryforward, plus tax losses offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply ordinary tax loss carryforward within the 5-year limit for China-source losses; trace and document that carried losses are not derived from foreign permanent establishments or shell structures; high-technology and small-medium science technology enterprises may use the 10-year carryforward only with the required certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed enterprise income tax before credits and preferential reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% headline rate, then reduce with the applicable preferential rate; claim foreign tax credit under Article 23 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law only for same-item China-source or foreign-source income and only where double taxation actually arises; retain foreign tax payment vouchers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable after tax credits, withholding credits, prepayments, and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that all withholding tax on distributed dividends, interest, royalties, and cross-border service payments has been declared; for non-resident shareholders receiving dividends, arrange payment only after confirmation of treaty relief or after withholding at the statutory 10% rate; report any withholding shortfall as a fatal compliance defect.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, or from RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 in serious circumstances; overdue tax accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid amount; failure to make quarterly prepayment may attract a 50%-500% penalty on the underpaid taxable amount under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law; deliberately false declarations are criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, punishable by up to 7 years imprisonment and asset confiscation; repeated violations trigger STA public blacklisting, travel bans, and enhanced audit supervision.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross China-source dividends paid to non-resident enterprises unless reduced by an applicable Double Taxation Treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before distribution, the non-resident shareholder must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence; the Chinese payer must file the withholding return and submit to the local State Taxation Administration a treaty benefits claim form, the TRC, a beneficial ownership self-assessment, an ownership chain diagram, articles of association, financial statements of the recipient, and an explanation of the active business or investment purpose; the applicant must demonstrate that the recipient is not a conduit, has substance and authority to deal with the shares, and satisfies the limitation-on-benefits clause; reduced withholding is effective only after the tax authority processes the claim, and remittance of the dividend before clearance may be recharacterized as non-treaty-exempt and subject to the statutory 10% rate plus late payment interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 10% on gross royalties and 10% on gross interest paid to non-resident enterprises; royalties additionally incur value-added tax at 6% plus urban maintenance and education surcharges in practice; treaty reduction commonly lowers royalty withholding to 5% and interest withholding to 7%-10% depending on the Double Taxation Treaty, always subject to the beneficial ownership test and Article 3 of the Model Tax Convention; intercompany interest may also be subject to thin-capitalization limitations under the special tax adjustment rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: China Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, RMB 50 million for intercompany loans, or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions; a Master File is required when aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion; contemporaneous transactional documentation must be filed with the annual corporate income tax return unless exempt by the annual total threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations, but the State Taxation Administration applies the substance-over-form doctrine, the beneficial ownership test, and Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, through which a transaction lacking reasonable commercial substance may be recharacterized; the JV must perform Core Income-Generating Activities in China, including operational decisions, client contracting, service delivery, and invoicing, and cannot outsource the substance to a shell affiliate in a zero-tax jurisdiction or in a treaty jurisdiction solely to obtain withholding benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Transfer Pricing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately submitting falsified contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, including a fabricated Local File and intercompany master service agreement, that understates China-source revenue and overstates royalty or management fees paid to a non-resident related party at non-arm's-length rates with the aim of shifting profit outside China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and Articles 118-120 of its Implementing Regulations authorize upward recharacterization and special tax adjustment; Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; failure to maintain usable transfer pricing documentation may result in a fine of RMB 10,000 plus interest and daily late payment surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under Article 20 of the Company Law if abuse of the legal person causes injury to the State's revenue claim; directors may become jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and interest; aggravated tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law carries imprisonment of three to seven years, criminal fines, asset confiscation, a judicial travel ban, and blacklisting by the tax authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Shopping / Beneficial Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or using a low-tax intermediary with no employees, premises, business activity, bank account independence, or decision-making power solely to hold shares of the JV and to receive dividends, interest, or royalties while claiming DTA reduced withholding through a tax residency certificate of the conduit country.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule in Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and STA Public Notice 2015 No. 35 authorize denial of treaty benefits and recharacterization of the conduit as an agent of the true beneficial owner; the payer must then withhold at the statutory 10% rate, plus interest and a 50%-500% penalty under the Tax Collection Administration Law; the intermediary may also be administratively dissolved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial ownership declarations or knowingly approve sham arrangements face civil restitution of the unpaid withholding tax; the sham shell treatment permits piercing of the corporate veil, making directors personally liable; criminal exposure includes tax evasion under Article 201 and money laundering under Article 191 of the Criminal Law, punishable by imprisonment of up to ten years, confiscation of personal property, a travel ban, and administrative blacklisting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / False Invoicing / Anti-Dumping Trade Defense Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing false VAT special invoices or materially under-invoicing consulting and service transactions in connection with anti-dumping defense engagements, misdeclaring the nature of services to disguise outbound transfers, or manipulating export prices and quantities to assist a client in circumventing antidumping duties while understating JV taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law treats this as tax evasion and imposes a penalty of 50%-500% of the amount underpaid; Article 205 of the Criminal Law punishes the false issuance of special VAT invoices with severe fines and imprisonment; the Anti-Dumping Regulations and Foreign Trade Law authorize retroactive collection of antidumping duties, fines, and revocation of operating licenses for aiding circumvention.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize, sign, or profit from false invoices are subject to criminal liability under Article 205, with punishments including life imprisonment in the gravest cases, unlimited fines, confiscation of personal assets, and disqualification from managerial positions; piercing the corporate veil permits courts to order directors to restore diverted assets and pay the JV's unpaid tax liabilities, and the authorities may impose a travel ban and blacklist the directors before commencement of criminal proceedings.
